s1.syndrome_frame: Hypertension with multisystem involvement and hemorrhagic stroke
salient_findings: Hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins
key_facts: Hypertension first noted at age 24 during pregnancy
Hypertension again at age 38 after basal ganglia hemorrhage
Splenomegaly diagnosed at age 21
Younger brother with similar splenomegaly finding
Normochromic microcytic anemia and thrombocytopenia on full blood examination
Low HDL and elevated triglycerides on lipid profile
Bilateral adrenal lesions on renal Doppler ultrasound and CT
Hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins on CT
No symptoms of adrenal hormone excess
Blood pressure controlled on a single antihypertensive agent

shortlist.label: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia
shortlist.why_kept: Hypertension, hemorrhagic stroke, and splenomegaly are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Systemic Mastocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Splenomegaly, anemia, thrombocytopenia, and low HDL are compatible with this condition

shortlist.label: Primary Myelofibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Splenomegaly, anemia, thrombocytopenia, and hepatosplenomegaly are features of this disease

shortlist.label: Polyarteritis Nodosa
shortlist.why_kept: Hypertension, hemorrhagic stroke, and multisystem involvement are possible manifestations of this condition

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Hypertension, anemia, thrombocytopenia, and multisystem involvement are consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with splenomegaly at a young age, normochromic microcytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and hepatosplenomegaly with dilated portal and splenic veins is consistent with Primary Myelofibrosis, a myeloproliferative neoplasm that can lead to extramedullary hematopoiesis and portal hypertension.

rejected.label: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia
rejected.why: While it could explain the basal ganglia hemorrhage, it does not account for the hematologic abnormalities and hepatosplenomegaly.

rejected.label: Systemic Mastocytosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with symptoms of mast cell activation, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Polyarteritis Nodosa
rejected.why: Usually presents with systemic vasculitis symptoms, which are not described in the case.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: Typically presents with a combination of autoimmune symptoms, which are not mentioned in the vignette.
